text: Literature is one of the most powerful forms of cultural diplomacy, said Deputy Minister Viktor Stoyanov in Thessaloniki (06.05.2026 21:27)

“Literature is one of the most powerful forms of cultural diplomacy,” said Acting Deputy Minister of Culture Viktor Stoyanov during the opening of the Thessaloniki International Book Fair, where Bulgaria is the guest of honor.

“Literature builds trust, encourages understanding, and creates lasting ties between peoples. Our presence in Thessaloniki is not only a celebration of Bulgarian literature — it is a celebration of the lasting friendship between Bulgaria and Greece. We are not only the closest neighbors and reliable allies in NATO and the EU — we are the closest friends in spirit, and our peoples share a deep respect and affection for one another,” Deputy Minister Stoyanov noted in his speech.
He pointed out that it is a privilege for Bulgaria to be the focus country of this year’s forum, as well as that this “embodies the spirit of dialogue and shared cultural horizons in our region.”

“Literary ties between Bulgaria and Greece are deep, vibrant, and enduring. For decades, our cultures have been in dialogue through poetry, prose, and translation. Greek poetry, with its philosophical depth and lyrical power, has left a lasting mark on Bulgarian literature. At the same time, Bulgarian authors have found in Greek readers a receptive and discerning audience,” he added.

The Deputy Minister noted the contribution of figures from the past and present, among whom he listed Stefan Gechev – diplomat, translator, and writer; Georgi Kufov – translator of Nikos Kazantzakis, Kostas Varnalis, and others. He also mentioned contemporary authors such as Yana Bukova, Georgi Gospodinov, Rene Karabash, Teodora Dimova, and Elena Alexieva, who have been translated into Greek.

Victor Stoyanov also drew attention to the important work of translators. “In just the last three years, more than 200 Bulgarian titles have been translated into foreign languages, with over ten of them translated into Greek. These figures reflect a clear and encouraging trend — Bulgarian literature is reaching an ever wider audience and building meaningful international connections,” he said.

The event was also attended by Nikolaos Bakounakis – Chairman of the Greek Foundation for Books and Culture, Christos Tzendemedis – Chairman of the Thessaloniki International Exhibition and Congress Center (TIF-HELEXPO S.A.), Lina Mendoni – Minister of Culture of Greece, Konstantinos Gkoulekas – Deputy Minister of the Interior of Greece responsible for Thrace and Macedonia, Athina Aidona – Governor of the Central Macedonia Region, Stelios Angeloudis – Mayor of Thessaloniki, Anton Markov – Consul General of Bulgaria in Thessaloniki, Teodora Dimova – Bulgarian writer, and others.
The official opening of the Bulgarian stand will take place on Thursday. “Literature Beyond Borders” is the central theme of Bulgaria’s participation.
